overall: It is very early morning in Atlanta (~01:50 ET) with the temperature flat at 80.6°F — the overnight low — and essentially no warming trend underway yet. A Heat Advisory is in effect through 8 PM EDT with expected heat index values of 105–108°F, consistent with a hot, humid airmass in place. Afternoon convective chances (30% PoP after 2 PM) introduce some uncertainty about whether storms could briefly suppress the peak, but conditions are otherwise strongly supportive of a very warm daytime high.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance is moderately spread: GFS is a clear high-side outlier at 96.3°F while ECMWF (93.0°F) aligns closely with the NWS official call of ~93°F; HRRR (91.3°F) and NBM (90.5°F) are slightly cooler, likely accounting for the afternoon storm chance. The META (fused) model strongly favors the 92–93°F bucket at 57.7%, which closely corroborates the NWS narrative and ECMWF, suggesting the GFS warm bias should be discounted.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence — NWS official 93°F, ECMWF 93.0°F, and the META model's 57.7% concentration in the 92–93°F bucket — points to a daily high in the 92–93°F range. The primary downside risk is an earlier-than-forecast convective onset clipping the afternoon peak (consistent with HRRR/NBM at 91–91.5°F), while the GFS 96.3°F scenario appears to be an outlier with low support from other guidance. Confidence in the 92–93°F even-bucket range is moderately high; the active even-bucket market's top bucket of 92–93F aligns well with the META signal.
